instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
While it heats, finely chop the onion, mince the 4 garlic cloves and cut the carrot into small dice. Dice half the bell pepper and chop the 3 tomatoes.
Add the 8 oz penne to the boiling water and cook for 8 to 9 minutes, until it's just tender with a little bite. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the penne.
Meanwhile, heat the 3 tbsp olive oil and the butter in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 20 seconds, until they smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until it's soft and golden.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Add the carrot, bell pepper and peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder, turmeric, garam masala and 1 tsp salt and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and the ketchup. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have broken down, the raw smell is gone and oil shows at the edges.
Pour in 1/2 cup of the pasta water and simmer for 2 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.

Crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the pan. Add the penne and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and cook on low for 2 minutes. If it looks dry, add a splash of the remaining pasta water.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes (Indian Healthy Recipes) cooks the onion and a little ginger and garlic in oil and butter after toasting cumin seeds, adds carrot, peas and bell pepper, then spices, tomatoes and a spoon of ketchup until the oil separates, and finishes with kasuri methi and the pasta in a thick sauce. My Ginger Garlic Kitchen and Subbu's Kitchen follow the same onion, tomato and capsicum base, with more cheese and Italian seasoning and a smaller tomato amount. This follows Swasthi's for the ratios, scaled up to serve 4 and with the optional cream and cheese left off. Chili powder is Kashmiri and kept low, so the base stays mild.
